correctness.rationale: Exact normalized path eigenvectors yield the determinant ratio for every complex spectral response with distinct selected multipliers. The three-mode absolute cosine polynomial and four-mode cubic give strict global comparisons, including all finite ties. The general theorem uses a uniform cosine-product inequality plus a nearest-integer argument. The standalone standard-library implementation independently builds graph matrices and checks 5641 assertions, but the analytical proof handles the infinite ranges. No unproved numerical extrapolation is required.

originality.rationale: The substantive new statement is a complete all-n classification of D-optimal single-vertex sensors for the first 2, 3 and 4 normalized-path eigenmodes, with exact exceptional ties, plus a general all-bandwidth sufficient theorem. The known general Vandermonde decomposition is a premise, not this extremal classification. The closest indexed full-spectrum endpoint theorem concerns a different (all-eigenmode) domain and cannot imply the inward-neighbor optimum for strict low bands. value.rationale: The first two through four graph Fourier bands are natural low-bandwidth reconstruction spaces, and determinant maximization is an intrinsic volume/noise-design criterion. The theorem precisely locates all optimal single vertices, including exceptional ties and a bandwidth-dependent reversal of full-spectrum endpoint placement; a general all-bandwidth sufficient path-size bound supplies structural extension. This is not merely a pointwise numerical experiment or a special case with no rationale.
